name: Pig kidney with a human lining
subtitle: an animal organ lined with your own cells

effects.effect: a guided enzyme cuts DNA at any spot spelled out by a short RNA
four genes turn an adult cell back into a stem cell that can become any tissue

effect: a guided enzyme cuts DNA at any spot spelled out by a short RNA
how: Animal organs are now edited to remove the sugars that trigger instant rejection, but the immune system still meets pig cells lining every blood vessel, and attacks them slowly for as long as the organ lasts. Those vessel linings can be stripped on the perfusion machine and reseeded with cells grown from the recipient, so the blood only ever touches the patient's own surface. The rest of the organ stays pig, hidden behind that lining.
obstacle: Reseeding every capillary in a kidney evenly, with cells that stay put under pressure, has never been achieved.
why: Both halves exist separately; a fully reseeded vascular bed is the unsolved step.
real: Partially decellularized rat kidneys reseeded with human endothelium perfused and made urine for ~90 min, and human discarded-kidney scaffolds have been seeded with hPSC endothelium, but no pig organ re-endothelialized with recipient cells and transplanted was found.
